regressions.source: Governor.execute/queue/cancel: proposalId = hashProposal(targets, values, calldatas, descriptionHash); state(proposalId) (GovernorTimelockControl: timelock.isOperationDone/isOperationPending), quorum, _cancel -> timelock.cancel(id)
regressions.issue: After the bytes[] encoding loop of hashProposal, the loop-carried pointer t (= the new mem[64]) has no lower bound, so every store through it may hit the scratch slots and slot 64. In these three functions 15 timelock/quorum calls lose their decoding (P2 3 -> 17), 12 'Governor: ...' reverts become raw memory (6 of them as 'revert with mem[mem[64] len 100], 0x6c00...'), and the proposal key prints as proposalSnapshot[concat(mem[0])] (P4 0 -> 15) and stor9[id] as uint64(stor[sha3(mem[0 len 64])]), right after 'mem[0] = sha3(...)' and with _29 holding that value.
regressions.rule: A pointer that starts at or above the free-memory pointer and only grows in a loop (t = t + ceil32(x) + 32) keeps that floor. With a floor of at least 128, stores through it never touch bytes 0..95, so mem[0], mem[32] and mem[64] still forward to the values stored there.
regressions.verified: text_check run --per-selector 16 (755/755 calls the same in both worlds: the semantics are unchanged); the display was checked by reading

improvements: castVoteBySig went from 411 to 159 lines: its 7 raw calls are decoded (getPastTotalSupply, isOperationDone/Pending, getPastVotes) and 13 raw reverts are now ECDSA/Governor messages. propose's raw calls are decoded. In castVote and castVoteWithReason, a dead getPastVotes call after an unconditional revert is dropped and the branch is flattened equivalently. VoteCast is logged with named arguments, and uint96 return checks read 'x == uint96(x)'. P6 16 -> 0.
notes: The diff is 2350 lines; I checked all 9 changed functions with per-function and normalized diffs. The one source loop (toHexString, 'while idx > 1') is still a while (6 inlined copies). The P2 and P4 increases are all in execute, cancel and queue, and come from the single cause in the regression. castVoteBySig and propose decreased.
summary: One medium regression: in execute, cancel and queue, the loop-advanced memory pointer loses its floor, so timelock calls, Governor revert strings and proposal-id mapping keys are no longer decoded (P2 13 -> 18, P4 3 -> 18). The text stays exact by text_check. castVoteBySig, propose and castVote improved a lot.
